Getting married next saturday. Any advice for life from other husbands out there?
For me and my wife we effectively live separate lives. She has her social circle, I have mine and never the two shall meet. Same for our interests.
I'm coming up on 15 years married. Just do what you want.

Never ever plan to "change" the other person. For everything they do that bugs you, you either accept it or you leave. (yes, 99.9% of the time the answer is "accept it"). If something really does bother you, talk to them about it, but don't be accusatory. There is no way they are doing it to bother you - it's just a different reality to them, and there is no "right" answer.

For example, let's say she never gives you a birthday card, and you grew up in a huge family where everyone hand-made birthday cards for every relative. To her it's simply not a big deal. If it really bothers you, then talk to her about it - but not as if she's doing something wrong. Talk to her about how it makes you feel (I know - cue the cookie-cutter marriage counselor routine, but it's true).

Learn to talk to each other about this stuff. Don't play silly little games like "I'm not going to return her call because I'm angry because she didn't kiss me goodbye this morning" - just talk to her and explain it. Learn to talk. Learn to talk and listen about feelings.

Never stop dating her.

Buy gifts. Both of you. We keep Amazon wish lists - not that we always buy from it, but it gives you a good idea about what kind of stuff they're looking at these days.

Never stop complimenting her. We've been married for 27 years, and when I just randomly say that she's pretty, she still lights up.

You are friends. Be friends. Talk like friends. Share like friends. My wife found my porn stash one time and organized it for me.

Go on vacations. Look for specials on plane fare and go somewhere neither of you have been for a four-day weekend.

Both of you should pull your credit reports and go over them together. Understand how each of you have structured your finances and make some decisions about how you will work your finances together.

This is a personal bias, but if you're going to have kids, have them right away. There is never a "convenient" time to have kids, but injecting children into the marriage early means your relationship solidifies around the kids. If you wait five years or more to have them, you'll have a married people routine that the kids will destabilize and it can be painful. Also, don't have an only child unless one of you was an only child.

And if you like this advice, just show it to her directly so she gets angry at me instead of you. :-D

Best wishes, and may you have many happy years together.

All of this. Can't emphasize enough how important open communication is. And it goes both ways, I like when she talks about her school work and interests even though I don't know what she's talking about half the time, but she loves to talk about it and that's enough to make me happy to listen.

Two things that helped me, one of them was something my mother told me about a week before I was married.

  1. If you don't go into this with the attitude that there is no way out of this marriage, you will most likely leave them later. You need to commit to this, commit so completely that you accept now that once you marry her you are doing it for life and giving her everything. IF you have the right woman, this idea won't scare you at all. If it gives you pause, then you may need to rethink some things. Not saying call it off, but it means you need to figure out what is making you uncertain.

  2. There WILL be hard times. Times when you're ready to put your fist through the wall even though you've never been in a fight in your life. You will get pissed off, you will feel like screaming, you will feel like you are never heard, and all you want is for her to understand you. It will be difficult, but put your feelings aside and assume she is feeling all those same things. Address those things for her, make her feel heard and that you are trying to understand her. Don't forget about your side of things, but for my marriage this has helped a ton.

As always, your mileage may vary. But it boils down to commit everything you are and have to the marriage, and don't let your anger get the best of you that you can't show her your love even when you are more angry than you've ever been.
